materials.title: Property Insurance Fundamentals
materials.contentText: Property insurance protects physical assets against covered perils such as fire, theft, and wind. Actual cash value reimburses replacement cost minus depreciation, while replacement cost reimburses without depreciation up to policy limits.

materials.title: Liability Coverage Basics
materials.contentText: Liability coverage responds to legal obligations for bodily injury and property damage caused by the insured. Insurers generally provide defense costs, settlement negotiations, and indemnity up to policy limits.

materials.title: Policy Structure and Conditions
materials.contentText: An insurance policy contains declarations, insuring agreement, conditions, exclusions, and endorsements. Conditions impose duties such as notice of loss and cooperation during claims.

materials.title: Insurance Regulation and Ethics
materials.contentText: State regulators oversee licensing, solvency, and market conduct. Ethical practice includes disclosure, suitability, fair claims handling, and anti-fraud compliance.

questions.questionText: What is the core purpose of property insurance?
options: To protect physical assets from covered losses
questions.correctAnswer: To protect physical assets from covered losses
questions.explanation: Property insurance is designed to cover covered damage or loss to physical property.

questions.questionText: How does replacement cost coverage differ from actual cash value?
options: Replacement cost pays without depreciation, ACV includes depreciation
They are identical under all policies
ACV always pays more than replacement cost
Replacement cost only applies to liability claims
questions.correctAnswer: Replacement cost pays without depreciation, ACV includes depreciation
questions.explanation: ACV accounts for depreciation while replacement cost typically does not, subject to policy terms.

questions.questionText: Liability coverage primarily applies when the insured is:
options: Legally responsible for injury or damage
questions.correctAnswer: Legally responsible for injury or damage
questions.explanation: Liability insurance responds to legal responsibility for third-party bodily injury or property damage.

questions.questionText: Which item is commonly included in liability policy benefits?
questions.explanation: Many liability forms include legal defense within policy provisions, subject to terms.

questions.questionText: Which section lists key coverage details such as named insured and limits?
questions.explanation: The declarations page contains core policy details including insured information and limits.

questions.questionText: What is the function of policy conditions?
options: State duties required to maintain coverage rights
questions.correctAnswer: State duties required to maintain coverage rights
questions.explanation: Conditions set obligations like prompt notice and cooperation during claims handling.

questions.questionText: Who generally regulates insurance licensing and market conduct in the US?
questions.explanation: Insurance is primarily regulated at the state level in the US.

questions.questionText: Which behavior best reflects ethical insurance practice?
questions.explanation: Ethical conduct requires transparency, suitability, and fair treatment of policyholders.
